ROCHA Sangguniang Bayan of Magdiwang Province of Romblon Dear Vice Mayor Rocha: This has reference to your letter dated 27 April 2018 requesting for the Department's opinion on the issue of whether or not Municipal Ordinance no. 2 series of 2014 of Sangguniang Bayan of Magdiwang, Province of Romblon, is already deemed approved. The letter query states that Sangguniang Bayan of Magdiwang, Province of Romblon, enacted Municipal Ordinance No. 2, Series of 2014. It was submitted to and received by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP) for its review on 02 February 2016 but per said letter, SP has yet to take an action. The issue submitted for this Department's legal opinion is whether or not the Municipal Ordinance No. 2, series of 2014 has already been deemed approved. This Department finds the provision on Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in Section 56 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, applicable.l The law 1 Section 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlala wigan. (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sanggunian panlungsod or sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days after the receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, the Sangguniang panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provincial attorney, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, within a period often (IO) days from receipt of the documents, inform the sangguniang panlalawigan in writing

provides that the reglementary period within which SP shall take an action on the review of ordinances is within 30 days after submission of the same. Accordingly, if SP had taken no action on the review of the subject municipal ordinance within 30 days after it was submitted, then the law is categorical that such ordinance is presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. This is consistent to our previous opinion in DILG Legal Opinion No. 14 series of 2018, which states: May we emphasize that the Department has been very consistent with its legal opinion that the phrase "take action" in Section 56(d) of R.A. 7160 should mean that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, within thirty days upon receipt of the copy OT the ordinance, should have rendered its legislative action in the form ofa resolution containing their approval or disapproval in whole or in part of the ordinance or resolution submitted to them for review. It is not enough that the measure be deliberated, debated and voted upon or simply referred to committee for further action because what is required of them is the enactment ofa legislative product that will formally and finally put to rest a given measure or issue. This legislative product is imbued with public interest so much so that the same shall serve as basis of the general public to rely upon in performing their respective obligations or asserting their rights in a given territory. Absent this product or document, all legislative debates are left as silent records becoming unenforceable as against thirdpersons. In sum, the Department's interpretation as to the mandatory character of the thirty day period is impelled by public policy considering that ordinances and similar legislative measures should attain stability at a given point in time. In the same vein, it is also settled that whenever power of his comments or recommendations, which may be considered by the sangguniang panlalawigan in making its decision. (c) If the sangguniang panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The Sangguniang panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. (d) Ifno action has been taken by the sarwuniangpanlalawigan within thirty (30) days after submission of such an ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid.

is given and it has to be exercised within a certain period of time, then such period is construed a limitation to such power. The foregoing eschews discretion and the same proceeds from a mandatory command. Indubitably, for it to be reviewed by SP, it shall be submitted to it. Conversely, the secretary to the sanggunian bayan (SB) shall, within three (3) days from approval, forward to SP copies of the approved ordinance for review. However, we herein note that Municipal Ordinance No. 2 series of 2014 was approved by the Sangguniang Bayan in 2014 and that it was only submitted to SP in 2016 despite the legal provision requiring for its submission within three (3) days after approval. Nevertheless, it has been our view that legislative measures such as ordinances are presumptively valid acts. Otherwise stated, they enjoy presumption Of regularity. It is a fundamental and familiar teaching that all reasonable doubts should be resolved in favor of the constitutionality of a statute.2 An act of the legislature, approved by the executive, is presumed to be within constitutional limitations.3 To justify the nullification ofa law, there must be a clear and unequivocal breach of the Constitution, not a doubtful and equivocal breach. 4 Accordingly, we herein conclude that said ordinance is already effective and presumed valid pending the review of the SP. However, the period within which the SP commences review shall be from the date of submission by the SB Secretary. The SB Secretary may be administratively liable for dereliction of duty for belated submission of the approved ordinance to the SP. This legal opinion is solely based on the facts stated in the letter-query. Very truly yours, By the authority of the Secretary L C.
